verdicts.reason: Real. The standard MSA dictionary form is فَلُوكَة falūka (Hans Wehr: falūka, pl. -āt, فَلَائِكُ falāʾik, 'felucca'); colloquial Egyptian is feluka/falūka. No dictionary gives fulūka with ḍamma, which looks like contamination from Quranic فُلْك. The word appears only on day 51 and in the nuzha example, so one replacement covers it; glosses ('felucca (a Nile sailing boat)', 'by felucca') stay.

verdicts.reason: Real as an inconsistency. ḥalwiyyāt can be defended by the nisba rule for حَلْوَى (dropping the alif maqṣūra), but the form in standard modern use and in learner dictionaries is حَلَوِيَّات ḥalawiyyāt (Wehr also gives ḥalwayāt; nobody vocalises ḥalwiyyāt in teaching texts), and the course itself teaches حَلَوِيَّات in the welcome scenario (culture note and lines[1]). One word should have one vocalisation; the fix moves to the course's own and the more standard form, so it cannot damage anything.
